claims.statement: Actor, UDI/device, notified-body and certificate, and market-surveillance modules of EUDAMED became mandatory on 28 May 2026.

Poland's URPL states that manufacturers must submit device information to EUDAMED before first placing a medical device on the EU market, while importers must verify the registration and add their details.
URPL set 27 November 2026 as the deadline for manufacturers to enter information on older devices that remained on the EU market after the mandatory-use date.

contrary_evidence: Manufacturers can use EUDAMED directly and many already employ regulatory consultants, so the standalone value must be data integrity and ongoing change control.
The largest one-time backfill deadline is close, making pure migration revenue temporary.

economics.acquisition_route: Pilot with two Polish regulatory consultants representing at least ten manufacturers, then add a free importer-verification report that generates manufacturer referrals
economics.founder_net_worth_path: Hypothesis: 450 manufacturers at 24000 PLN recurring revenue yields 10.8m PLN ARR; at 24% EBITDA, 4x EBITDA, and 65% founder ownership, equity could exceed 6.7m PLN in years 6-8. Validate the addressable lean-team segment and avoid double-counting retained cash.
economics.founder_time: 3-5 hours per day during a narrow Class I/low-complexity pilot, with a contracted medical-device regulatory professional approving production rules
economics.gross_margin_basis: Hypothesis: 68-82% once validations are rule-driven; keep mandatory human release review in the price
economics.payback: Hypothesis: 9-15 months if 15 manufacturers average 14000 PLN first-year revenue; validate liability insurance and consultant margin
economics.pricing: Hypothesis: 4500-12000 PLN onboarding per Basic UDI-DI family plus 9000-30000 PLN annual maintenance per manufacturer; partner volume discounts
economics.retention_or_repeat: Device records, actor links, certificates, and labels change over long market lifecycles; audit history and product hierarchies are costly to reconstruct

fingerprint.compounding_advantage: A structured history of accepted device records, EMDN mappings, certificate relationships, and validation failures reduces error rates and creates high switching costs
fingerprint.customer: Polish and Central European micro and small medical-device and IVD manufacturers, authorised representatives, and importers with lean regulatory teams
fingerprint.distribution_mechanism: White-label through regulatory consultancies and authorised representatives; importer verification requests bring additional manufacturers into the system
fingerprint.offer_and_business_model: Human-verified product-master-data validation, UDI hierarchy management, EUDAMED submission support, change monitoring, and immutable approval evidence
fingerprint.payer_and_paid_event: The manufacturer pays per product family at first release and an annual maintenance fee; representatives pay for multi-manufacturer workspaces
fingerprint.problem_trigger: A new device is about to be placed on the EU market, an existing device must be backfilled, or a certificate, actor, label, or importer record changes

founder_fit: Leverages health-domain interest, data science, and meticulous evidence workflows
AI can assist extraction while a human retains regulated approval authority
A consultant channel avoids camera-based marketing and constant broad sales
A narrow pilot is possible within the founder's time and capital constraints
risks: A wrong device, UDI, certificate, or actor relationship could block market access or create regulatory exposure.
Consultancies may treat the product as a threat rather than a channel.
EUDAMED interface changes could require frequent maintenance.

structure.control_point: the verified UDI/device record required before first EU market placement and maintained through product changes
structure.critical_dependency: near-perfect device hierarchy and certificate mapping plus lawful, reliable access to EUDAMED submission workflows

thesis: Offer a managed data-release desk for small Polish and Central European medical-device and IVD manufacturers whose product master data must reconcile across their quality system, Basic UDI-DI hierarchy, EMDN coding, certificates, labels, importers, and EUDAMED records. The product acts as a pre-market release gate: it validates the record, routes exceptions to an accountable human, submits or prepares the authoritative update, and retains evidence of who approved what. Enter through medical-device regulatory consultants, authorised representatives, and UDI issuing organisations, which each aggregate many manufacturers. The durable asset is a versioned device-to-certificate-to-actor graph and an error corpus that makes subsequent registrations and change control faster across the EU.
title: EUDAMED UDI Release Desk
uncertainties: Submission/API access available to an authorised service acting for manufacturers
Number of small manufacturers with enough device complexity and budget
Professional-liability, quality-system, and validation requirements for the service
